title: Security review for quickstart templates: secrets handling, dependency scanning, and unsafe tool patterns audit
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Validate that v1 quickstart templates ship with secure-by-default guidance and guardrails (local dev + container + k8s), and do not demonstrate unsafe patterns that create support/security escalations.

Scope
1) Secrets handling
- Ensure templates do not encourage committing secrets or putting long-lived keys in plain text.
- Ensure .env usage is constrained to local development with clear warnings; production path should point to secret managers (K8s Secrets, AWS/GCP secret managers, Vault, etc.).
- Confirm structured logs do not print secrets; confirm any config debug logs are safe.

2) Dependency scanning + pinning
- Ensure dependencies are pinned and lockfiles are committed.
- Add/confirm automated scanning: GitHub Advanced Security/Dependabot (or Renovate), secret scanning, and basic SAST where applicable.
- Ensure CI fails on critical vuln threshold and prevents known-insecure dependency ranges.

3) Unsafe tool patterns audit (agents template and combined RAG+agent)
- Validate tool allow-list is explicit; prohibit “arbitrary code execution” tools and unrestricted network/file access by default.
- Ensure tool inputs/outputs are validated (JSON schema), tool timeouts enforced, and errors handled safely (no retries that cause repeated side effects; no leaking tool output with sensitive content).
- Confirm prompt-injection mitigations are documented (retrieval content is untrusted; do not let retrieved text override tool policies).

Acceptance criteria
- Written review findings captured below, with actionable fixes merged or tracked as follow-up tickets.
- Quickstart repo includes:
  - Secret scanning (pre-commit/CI) + documented local-dev .env pattern
  - Pinned deps / lockfiles + automated dependency alerts
  - Agent tool calling patterns: allow-list, timeouts, schema validation, safe error handling
  - Logging guidance: PII and secrets redaction note + correlation IDs without sensitive payloads
- Sign-off from Security stakeholders: Naomi Feldman (product), Marcus Lin (secure defaults), Kevin Osei (audit/SIEM guidance).

Findings (initial review)
A) Secrets handling
- Good: Templates already use env vars and do not embed keys in code.
- Gaps:
  1. README examples included copy/paste snippets that could lead users to paste keys into shell history and/or commit .env accidentally.
  2. Docker Compose sample mounted local .env by default without warning banner.
  3. One debug log statement printed full Redwood base URL + headers object (risk: accidental Authorization header logging if users add it).
- Required fixes:
  - Add a prominent “Never commit .env” warning + .gitignore entries verified.
  - Provide “.env.example” with placeholder values and comments; include KEY ROTATION note.
  - Add a minimal “prod” section: K8s Secret manifest snippet + recommendation to use external secrets operator.
  - Ensure config loader scrubs values for keys matching /(key|token|secret|authorization)/i when printing debug output.

B) Dependency scanning + pinning
- Python:
  - Gap: requirements.txt was version-ranged in one template; ingestion worker had an unpinned transitive dependency.
  - Fix: use lock (pip-tools compiled requirements.txt or uv lock) + CI check that lock is up to date.
- TypeScript:
  - Good: package-lock.json exists.
  - Gap: scripts allowed “npm install” without “npm ci” in CI.
- Repo automation:
  - Gap: no secret scanning pre-commit config; no dependency update automation defined.
  - Fix: add:
    - gitleaks (or equivalent) in CI
    - Dependabot/Renovate config
    - Trivy (filesystem) or npm audit threshold + pip-audit in CI (fail on critical/high in direct deps; warn on transitive with waiver process)

C) Unsafe tool patterns audit
- Good:
  - Tool wrapper implements timeouts.
  - Tool output JSON schema validation exists.
- Gaps:
  1. Default tool set included an example “http_fetch(url)” without domain allow-list, SSRF protections, or egress guidance.
  2. Error messages returned to client included raw tool exception text (could leak internal network info or stack traces).
  3. No explicit warning that retrieved documents can be prompt-injection vectors (“RAG content is untrusted input”).
  4. Idempotency guidance for tools with side effects was too light; retry behavior could duplicate side effects.
- Required fixes:
  - Replace http_fetch default example with a stubbed “KnowledgeBase.search()” or safe “GET to allow-listed domains only” example.
  - Add default tool policy object: allow_list, deny_list, timeout_ms, max_response_bytes.
  - Sanitize tool errors returned to end users (map to error codes; keep raw errors in logs only).
  - Document “tool side effects” and require idempotency keys for write operations.

Remediation plan
- Bundle fixes into one hardening PR to redwood-quickstarts.
- Update docs to align (avoid drift): ensure docs-site snippets reference the same safe patterns.
- Add CI gates (do not ship without passing).

Links / artifacts
- Confluence: security baseline for templates (secrets + local dev policy)
- Confluence: agent tool calling guidelines (allow-lists, timeouts, validation)
- GitHub PRs expected:
  - Security hardening pass (dependency pinning, secret scanning config, safer default logging)

Out of scope (explicit)
- Building a full secrets manager integration library.
- Guaranteeing compliance; only provide patterns and guardrails.

Follow-ups (if not completed by launch)
- Add SBOM generation (CycloneDX) for published template releases.
- Add pre-commit hooks doc + one-command installer for contributors.
